title: View the Ontology
description: Open Ontology and browse the different concepts.
annotation: In the navbar, open Ontology and browse the different terminology. Terms are grouped together as concepts. For example, Capability lists the names, codes, categories, roles etc. that characterise a Capability.

title: Propose a new code
description: Add a new code under a concept type.
annotation: Under the concept type, enter a code and a label, then choose Add. A new code is a proposal until the Ontology Manager approves it. Approval is not part of this demo: the Ontology Manager reviews each proposed code and decides whether it becomes canonical.

title: Find the pending code
description: Open Ontology Approvals and find the pending code.
annotation: Open Ontology Approvals and find the code you proposed. This is where the Ontology Manager decides which codes become canonical.

title: Approve the code
annotation: Choose Approve on the pending code. Approval makes the code canonical, so Packs that use it can be published.

title: Reject the code
description: Reject a pending code with a reason.
annotation: Enter a reason on the pending code and choose Reject. A rejected code is not canonical, and the reason tells the author what to change.

title: Compose a code from an existing code
description: Compose a code from an existing code.
annotation: Choose Compose, select the source code, choose specialization or override, enter the new code and choose Compose. A composed code builds on an existing one, so the vocabulary grows without starting again.

title: Ontology provides the semantic foundation for the platform
annotation: Ontology defines the shared semantic vocabulary used by a Software Engineering Unit (SEU). Its purpose is to ensure that all Participants, Deliverables, Knowledge, Evidence, Decisions and Packs operate using a common understanding of engineering concepts. Tenants can override Platform Ontology or define new ones. Demo does not allow this feature.

title: The Registry lists every declared Pack
description: Find the Pack in the Registry - note
annotation: A Pack carries the practice an organisation chooses to follow. A Template / Profile selects the Packs it uses.

title: Find the Pack in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Packs, and find the Pack.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Packs. Packs are grouped into different categories. You can also view them grouped in different states. Packs can contribute to Capabilites, Services etc. They can also be declared as independent behaviors that can be added to Templates/Profiles. **Example**: - C Engineering Practices Pack contributes to "Constructing software systems " and "Reviewing engineering work " Capabilities. - Banking, Payments & Capital Markets Domain Practices Pack is an independent Pack that can be added to any Template/Profile used for delivering software in the Banking domain.

title: A Pack is the **fundamental unit of extension** within the Platform.
annotation: Packs enable organisations to tailor SEUs to specific engineering practices, standards, policies, business domains, technologies, compliance requirements and integration environments while preserving architectural stability.

title: Open Pack Authoring
description: Open SDK / Pack Authoring and choose New Pack.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Pack Authoring. Choose New Pack. Entered information has to comply to the Pack Schema so it can be converted to a computable configuration.

title: A new Pack starts as a Draft
annotation: A Pack is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published.

title: Create the draft
description: Enter code, name, category, version and classification, then create the draft.
annotation: Enter a code, a name, a category, a version and an installation classification. Choose Create draft. A new Pack starts as a Draft.

title: Contributions give the Pack its content
annotation: Contributions are the checklists, Obligations and other definitions that a Pack adds. A JSON document can supply them together.

title: Add the contributions
description: Paste a Pack document into the JSON import card and import it.
annotation: On the draft, find the JSON import card. Paste the Pack document and choose Import. The contributions give the Pack its content.

title: A Pack can be composed from existing Packs
annotation: Composition builds a new Pack from existing Packs by a Composition Strategy, such as Specialization (an exact copy of one parent), Merge, Union or Override. The result is a starting point for the draft, not a lock.

title: Compose the Pack from source Packs
description: Choose a Composition Strategy and the source Pack(s) on the draft, save, then choose Compose from sources.
annotation: On the draft, choose a Composition Strategy and one or more source Packs, and save. Then choose Compose from sources. The draft is pre-filled from the sources. Review the result and edit it as needed.

title: Validation checks the Pack before it is published
annotation: Validation checks that the Pack is complete and consistent. A Pack with a new code waits at Validated until the Ontology accepts the code.

title: Validate the Pack
annotation: Choose Validate Pack. Validation checks that the Pack is complete and consistent.

title: Publishing makes the Pack available
annotation: A published Pack is Active and can be selected by a Profile.

title: Publish the Pack
annotation: Choose Publish. A published Pack is Active and can be selected by a Profile.

title: A Template is the engineering blueprint for delivering software
description: Find the Template in the Registry - note
annotation:
A Template groups the typical processes that a type of work needs, such as the domain, compliance and technology Packs. A Profile is built on a Template. Templates describe the engineering structure required  and the default engineering assets that should be available when the SEU is commissioned.

ArchVault Digital Shelf is meant for mobiles. Check the Template Registry for a mobile platform development.

title: Find the Template in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Templates and find the Template.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Template Registry. Each card shows the Template and the Packs it composes. Search for mobile and view the

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Template
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Template. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Template
description: Copy an existing Template into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Template. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: Authoring is where a Template is declared
annotation: Template Authoring is where an organisation declares the Template for its own type of work. The Registry lists the Templates already declared.

title: Open Template Authoring
description: Open SDK / Template Authoring and choose New Template.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Template Authoring. Choose New Template.

title: A new Template starts as a Draft
annotation: A Template is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published.

title: Create the draft
description: Enter the Template details and create the draft.
annotation: Enter a code, a name and a version for the Template. Choose Create draft. A new Template starts as a Draft.

title: The Packs make up the Template
annotation: The Packs selected here define the practice the Template carries. A Pack declares the practice. The Template chooses which Packs apply.

title: Select the Packs
description: Select the Packs the Template composes and save the draft.
annotation: On the draft, select the Packs for each category, such as domain, compliance and technology. Choose Save.

title: Validation checks the Template before it is published
annotation: Validation checks that the Template is complete and its Packs are compatible.

title: Validate the Template
annotation: Choose Validate Template. Validation checks that the Template is complete and consistent.

title: Publishing makes the Template available
annotation: A published Template is Active and can be used by a Profile.

title: Publish the Template
annotation: Choose Publish. A published Template is Active and can be used by a Profile.

title: A Profile fits a Template to a team
description: Find the Profile in the Registry - note
annotation: A Profile selects the Packs a team uses and sets the parameters of its Template. A Software Engineering Unit is commissioned with one Profile.

title: Find the Profile in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Profiles, and find the Profile.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Profiles. Each card shows the Profile and the Packs it uses.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Profile
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Profile. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Profile
description: Copy an existing Profile into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Profile. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: Authoring is where a Profile is declared
annotation: Profile Authoring is where an organisation declares the Profile for its own team. The Registry lists the Profiles already declared.

title: Open Profile Authoring
description: Open SDK / Profile Authoring and choose New Profile.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Profile Authoring. Choose New Profile.

title: A new Profile starts as a Draft
annotation: A Profile is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published.

title: Create the draft
description: Enter the Profile details and create the draft.
annotation: Enter a code, a name and a version for the Profile. Choose Create draft. A new Profile starts as a Draft.

title: The Packs make up the Profile
annotation: The Packs selected here define the practice the Profile applies. A Pack declares the practice. The Profile chooses which Packs apply.

title: Select the Packs
description: Select the Packs the Profile uses and save the draft.
annotation: On the draft, select the Packs for each category, such as domain, compliance and technology, and the optional Packs. Choose Save.

title: A Profile can set a service level
annotation: A service level states the target a Service is held to, such as a response time. The Profile can set it for the team without changing the Pack.

title: Change the service level
description: Set the service level on the Profile and save.
annotation: On the draft, set the service level for the Service and choose Save.

title: Validation checks the Profile before it is published
annotation: Validation checks that the Profile is complete and its Packs are compatible.

title: Validate the Profile
annotation: Choose Validate Profile. Validation checks that the Profile is complete and consistent.

title: Publishing makes the Profile available
annotation: A published Profile is Active and can be selected when a Software Engineering Unit is commissioned.

title: Publish the Profile
annotation: Choose Publish. A published Profile is Active and can be used to commission a Software Engineering Unit.

title: Engineering competencies are available in the Capability, Service and Deliverable Registry.
description: Find the Capability Definition in the Registry - note
annotation:
Capabilities represent the engineering competencies required to deliver software within a Software Engineering Unit (SEU).

A Capability defines **what engineering function must be performed**, independent of who or what performs it.

A Capability provides a guaranteed Service which includes the expected Deliverables and Service Levels.

title: Find the Capability Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry and view the Capability Definitions.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Capability Registry. Each card shows the Capability Definition and links to the Service it provides.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Capability Definition
annotation: Copying is the quickest way to derive a Capability Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be edited before it is published. A new Capability can also be created from scratch. A new Capability needs a new code. The code must be an approved Ontology concept before the Capability can be published. Also create the corresponding Service and Deliverables to complete the definition.

title: Copy the Capability Definition
description: Copy a Capability Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Capability Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Capability Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Capability Definition - note
annotation: A Capability Definition is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published. A published Capability Definition is Active.

title: Author a new Capability Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Capability Definition in SDK / Capability Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Capability Authoring. Choose New, enter the details and create the draft. Save it, choose Validate, then Publish.

title: The Registry lists every Deliverable Definition
description: Find the Deliverable Definition in the Registry - note
annotation: A Deliverable Definition declares a kind of work product, such as a specification or a design, that a Software Engineering Unit produces.

title: Find the Deliverable Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Deliverable Definitions, and find the Deliverable Definition.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Deliverable Definitions. Each card shows the Deliverable Definition and its version.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Deliverable Definition
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Deliverable Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Deliverable Definition
description: Copy a Deliverable Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Deliverable Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Deliverable Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Deliverable Definition - note
annotation: A Deliverable Definition is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published. A published Deliverable Definition is Active.

title: Author a new Deliverable Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Deliverable Definition in SDK / Deliverable Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Deliverable Authoring. Choose New, enter the details and create the draft. Save it, choose Validate, then Publish.

title: The Registry lists every Service Definition
description: Find the Service Definition in the Registry - note
annotation: A Service Definition declares a service that a Software Engineering Unit offers or consumes, with its service levels.

title: Find the Service Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Service Definitions, and find the Service Definition.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Service Definitions. Each card shows the Service Definition and its version.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Service Definition
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Service Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Service Definition
description: Copy a Service Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Service Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Service Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Service Definition - note
annotation: A Service Definition is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published. A published Service Definition is Active.

title: Author a new Service Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Service Definition in SDK / Service Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Service Authoring. Choose New, enter the details and create the draft. Save it, choose Validate, then Publish.

title: The Registry lists every Policy Definition
description: Find the Policy Definition in the Registry - note
annotation: A Policy Definition declares a rule that applies across Packs, such as a limit or a required check.

title: Find the Policy Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Policy Definitions, and find the Policy Definition.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Policy Definitions. Each card shows the Policy Definition and its version.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Policy Definition
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Policy Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Policy Definition
description: Copy a Policy Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Policy Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Policy Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Policy Definition - note
annotation: A Policy Definition is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published. A published Policy Definition is Active.

title: Author a new Policy Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Policy Definition in SDK / Policy Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Policy Authoring. Choose New, enter the details and create the draft. Save it, choose Validate, then Publish.

title: A Transition Definition declares one state change
description: Author a new Transition Definition - note
annotation: A Transition Definition declares one move from one state to another for an entity, and the authority needed to make it. It starts as a Draft until it is validated and published.

title: Author a new Transition Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Transition Definition in SDK / Transition Definition Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Transition Definition Authoring. Choose New, enter the details and create the draft. Save it, choose Validate, then Publish.

title: A schema describes the fields of a definition
description: Find the schemas in the Schema Registry - note
annotation: The Schema Registry lists the schema for each kind of definition. The authoring forms are built from these schemas.

title: Find the schemas in the Schema Registry
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Schema Registry. Each schema describes the fields of one kind of definition.

title: Participants are the people and systems that do the work
annotation: A Participant is a person or a system that can fulfil a Capability. The Registry lists the Participants available to the tenant.

title: Find the Participants
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Participants. Each entry is a person or system that can be given work.

title: A noun names what authority applies to
annotation: Authority is expressed as a noun and a verb, such as pack and publish. The noun is the entity. The verb is the action.

title: Open the authority nouns
annotation: Open Authority, then Nouns. A noun names a kind of entity that authority applies to.

title: A new noun extends the authority vocabulary
annotation: A noun added here can be combined with the verbs to form a badge.

title: Add a noun
annotation: On the Nouns page, enter a noun and choose Add.

title: A verb names an action
annotation: The verb is the action a badge permits, such as define, approve or publish.

title: Open the authority verbs
annotation: Open Authority, then Verbs. A verb names an action that authority permits.

title: A new verb extends the authority vocabulary
annotation: A verb added here can be combined with the nouns to form a badge.

title: Add a verb
annotation: On the Verbs page, enter a verb and choose Add.

title: The mapping pairs a noun with a verb
description: Open the noun and verb mapping - note
annotation: Each pairing is a badge. The mapping states which actions apply to which entity, and whether a person or the system triggers them.

title: Open the noun and verb mapping
description: Open the noun and verb mapping.
annotation: Open Authority, then Mapping. Each row pairs a noun with a verb and shows how the transition is triggered.

title: A new mapping creates a badge
description: Map a verb to a noun - note
annotation: Mapping a verb to a noun creates the badge that permits that action on that entity.

title: Map a verb to a noun
description: Map a verb to a noun.
annotation: On the Mapping page, choose a noun and a verb and choose Add.

title: The trigger states who starts the transition
description: Change the trigger of a mapping - note
annotation: A manual trigger means a person starts the transition. An automatic trigger means the platform does.

title: Change the trigger of a mapping
description: Change the trigger of a mapping.
annotation: On the Mapping page, choose a mapping and change its trigger. Choose Save.

title: A transition definition declares one state change
annotation: It names the entity, the state it moves from and to, and the badge needed to make the move.

title: Open a transition definition
annotation: Open a transition definition from the list to see the states it moves between and the authority it needs.

title: Editing changes how an entity may move
annotation: A change here changes which badge is needed for a state change, and what the change triggers.

title: Edit a transition definition
description: Edit a transition definition and save.
annotation: Choose Edit, change the definition and choose Save.

title: A badge gives a user the authority to act
description: Grant a badge to a user - note
annotation: A user can make a state change only when they hold the badge it needs. The Tenant Administrator grants badges to users.

title: Grant a badge to a user
description: Open Tenant Users and grant a badge to a user.
annotation: Open Tenant Administration, then Users. Choose a user and grant a badge.

title: An Objective states what the work is for
annotation: An Objective states an outcome the organisation wants. Objectives form a hierarchy, and a Software Engineering Unit is commissioned to deliver one.

title: Find the Objectives
annotation: In the navbar, open Objectives. The list shows the Objectives and where each sits in the hierarchy.

title: A new Objective starts as a proposal
annotation: The Objective waits in its first state until a person with the authority activates it.

title: Propose an Objective
description: Choose New under a parent Objective, enter the details and create it.
annotation: Choose New under a parent Objective. Enter the details and create it. A new Objective is a proposal until it is activated.

title: An Objective can be broken into child Objectives
annotation: Child Objectives split a larger outcome into parts that can each be delivered and tracked.

title: Open an Objective
annotation: Choose an Objective in the list to see its details and its child Objectives.

title: An Objective can be refined
annotation: Edits change the proposal. They are recorded against the Objective.

title: Edit the Objective
annotation: Choose Edit, change the details and choose Save.

title: Moving changes where an Objective sits
annotation: The Objective keeps its content and takes a new place in the hierarchy.

title: Move the Objective
description: Move the Objective under another parent.
annotation: Choose Move and select the new parent Objective.

title: Comments record the discussion
annotation: Comments stay with the Objective so that later readers can see why it changed.

title: Comment on the Objective
annotation: Enter a comment on the Objective and choose Add.

title: Activate is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Activation makes the Objective current. A Software Engineering Unit can then be commissioned for it.

title: Activate the Objective
annotation: Choose Activate on the Objective and confirm.

title: Supersede is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Supersession replaces an Objective with a newer one. The old Objective stays on record.

title: Supersede the Objective
annotation: Choose Supersede on the Objective and confirm.

title: Retire is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Retirement ends an Objective that is no longer pursued.

title: Retire the Objective
annotation: Choose Retire on the Objective and confirm.

title: Archive is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Archiving removes an ended Objective from active lists. It stays on record.

title: Archive the Objective
annotation: Choose Archive on the Objective and confirm.

title: Reject is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Rejection ends a proposal that will not go ahead.

title: Reject the Objective
annotation: Choose Reject on the Objective and confirm.

title: Only a draft can be deleted
annotation: A draft has not been acted on. Once an Objective has moved on, it is retired or archived instead.

title: Delete a draft Objective
annotation: Choose Delete on a draft Objective and confirm.

title: Commissioning has preconditions
description: Check the Objective is ready to commission - note
annotation: An Objective is commissioned only when it is active and its Template and Profile are in place.

title: Check the Objective is ready to commission
description: Check the Objective is ready to commission.
annotation: Choose Validate commission. The check lists anything that must be fixed first.

title: The Evidence-Based Model is composed from Packs
annotation: Composition joins the Packs of the Template and Profile into the model that governs the Software Engineering Unit.

title: Compose the Evidence-Based Model
description: Compose the Evidence-Based Model for the Objective.
annotation: Choose Compose Evidence-Based Model, select the Template and Profile, and compose.

title: A Software Engineering Unit does the work
description: Find the Software Engineering Units - note
annotation: A Software Engineering Unit is commissioned for an Objective. It carries the Capabilities, Deliverables, Obligations and Evidence of the work.

title: Find the Software Engineering Units
annotation: In the navbar, open SEUs. Each entry is a unit commissioned to deliver an Objective.

title: Commissioning creates the unit
description: Commission a Software Engineering Unit - note
annotation: Commissioning composes the Evidence-Based Model and creates the Capabilities, Deliverables and Obligations the model calls for.

title: Commission a Software Engineering Unit
description: Choose New SEU, select the Objective, Template and Profile, and commission.
annotation: Choose New SEU, select the Objective, the Template and the Profile, and choose Commission.

title: The unit page shows the whole picture
description: Open a Software Engineering Unit - note
annotation: The page shows the unit's state and what it must deliver, who is working on it and what is outstanding.

title: Open a Software Engineering Unit
annotation: Choose a unit in the list to see its state, Capabilities, Deliverables and Obligations.

title: A unit has a lifecycle
description: Move the unit to its next state - note
annotation: A unit moves through states such as validated, suspended and retired. Each move needs the matching badge.

title: Move the unit to its next state
description: Move the SEU to its next lifecycle state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the unit, such as Validate, Suspend or Resume.

title: The model governs the unit
annotation: The Evidence-Based Model is authoritative for the unit until it is superseded through a governed recomposition.

title: Open the Evidence-Based Model
description: Open the Evidence-Based Model of the SEU.
annotation: Open the Evidence-Based Model from the unit page. It lists the Packs that govern the unit.

title: The model is validated and then activated
description: Move the model to its next state - note
annotation: Activation makes the model the one the unit follows.

title: Move the model to its next state
description: Move the Evidence-Based Model to its next state.
annotation: On the model page, choose Validate or Activate.

title: A Capability is fulfilled by a Participant
annotation: The Participant takes on the Capability and can then be given work.

title: Fulfil a Capability
description: Fulfil a Capability with a Participant.
annotation: On the unit page, choose a Capability and select a Participant to fulfil it.

title: A Participant can be replaced
annotation: The work stays with the Capability. A different Participant takes over.

title: Replace the Participant
description: Replace the Participant on a Capability.
annotation: Choose Replace beside the Participant and select another.

title: Release returns the Capability to the pool
annotation: The Capability is no longer fulfilled until another Participant takes it.

title: Release a Capability
annotation: Choose Release on the Capability.

title: Work is queued for Participants
annotation: The queue lists what has to be done next. Work is generated from the Evidence-Based Model.

title: Open the work queue
description: Open the work queue of the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, open the work queue. It lists the work items waiting for a Participant.

title: Completing work moves the unit forward
annotation: A completed item can release the next item and update the state of the Deliverable or Obligation it belongs to.

title: Complete a work item
annotation: Choose Complete on a work item.

title: A Deliverable has a lifecycle
annotation: A Deliverable is a work product. It moves from draft through review to approval.

title: Move a Deliverable on
description: Move a Deliverable to its next state.
annotation: On the unit page, choose a state change on a Deliverable.

title: An Obligation is something the unit must satisfy
annotation: An Obligation moves through analysis, work, resolution, verification and closure, each with its own badge.

title: Move an Obligation on
description: Move an Obligation to its next state.
annotation: On the unit page, choose a state change on an Obligation, such as Start or Resolve.

title: A revision keeps the history
annotation: The earlier version of the Obligation stays on record.

title: Revise an Obligation
annotation: Choose Revise on the Obligation and change its details.

title: Evidence shows an Obligation was met
annotation: Evidence is the record that an Obligation has been satisfied.

title: Record Evidence
annotation: Choose Record Evidence on an Obligation, enter the details and save.

title: Evidence is checked before it is accepted
annotation: Validation checks the Evidence against what the Obligation requires.

title: Validate the Evidence
annotation: Choose Validate on the Evidence.

title: Evidence has a lifecycle
annotation: Accepted Evidence can close an Obligation.

title: Move the Evidence on
description: Move the Evidence to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Evidence, such as Accept or Reject.

title: Links show what the Evidence supports
annotation: A link connects the Evidence to another Obligation or record.

title: Link the Evidence
description: Link the Evidence to another record.
annotation: Choose Link on the Evidence and select the record.

title: Knowledge keeps what the unit has learned
annotation: A Knowledge item records a lesson or a reusable finding from the work.

title: Record a Knowledge item
annotation: Choose Record Knowledge, enter the details and save.

title: Knowledge is reviewed before it is shared
description: Move the Knowledge item on - note
annotation: A Knowledge item is proposed, validated, accepted and then published.

title: Move the Knowledge item on
description: Move the Knowledge item to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Knowledge item, such as Propose or Publish.

title: Scope decides who can see the Knowledge
annotation: Promotion widens the Knowledge from the unit to a wider audience.

title: Promote the Knowledge item
description: Promote the Knowledge item to a wider scope.
annotation: Choose Promote scope on the Knowledge item.

title: Knowledge Capital is the organisation's shared learning
annotation: It collects published Knowledge from every unit.

title: Open Knowledge Capital
annotation: In the navbar, open Knowledge Capital. It lists the Knowledge the organisation has gathered.

title: A Decision records a choice and its reason
annotation: A Decision stays with the unit so that the reason for a choice can be found later.

title: Record a Decision
annotation: Choose Record Decision, enter the details and save.

title: A Decision is reviewed and approved
annotation: A Decision is analysed, proposed, reviewed, approved and applied.

title: Move the Decision on
description: Move the Decision to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Decision, such as Review or Approve.

title: External parties are part of the work
annotation: An external interaction records a request to or a reply from a party outside the unit.

title: Record an external interaction
annotation: Choose Record interaction, enter the details and save.

title: An interaction has a lifecycle
annotation: The interaction moves from requested to answered to closed.

title: Move the interaction on
description: Move the external interaction to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the interaction.

title: A review examines the work
annotation: A review checks a Deliverable or a stage of the work and records what it finds.

title: Open the reviews
description: Open the reviews of the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, open Reviews.

title: A review has a subject
annotation: The review is opened against the work it examines.

title: Start a review
annotation: Choose Start review and select what is reviewed.

title: A review ends with an outcome
annotation: The review is completed when its findings are recorded.

title: Move the review on
description: Move the review to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the review.

title: A Finding records a problem found
annotation: A Finding states what is wrong and how serious it is.

title: Raise a Finding
description: Raise a Finding in the review.
annotation: In the review, choose Raise Finding, enter the details and save.

title: A Finding is handled until it is closed
annotation: A Finding is accepted, resolved or dismissed.

title: Move the Finding on
description: Move the Finding to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Finding.

title: A Finding can become work
description: Convert the Finding into an Obligation - note
annotation: Converting a Finding creates an Obligation, so that the fix is tracked to closure.

title: Convert the Finding into an Obligation
description: Convert the Finding into an Obligation.
annotation: Choose Convert on the Finding.

title: Attention items flag what needs notice
annotation: A Blocker stops work. A Risk may stop it.

title: Raise an Attention item
description: Raise an Attention item (Blocker or Risk).
annotation: On the unit page, choose Raise Attention, select Blocker or Risk, enter the details and save.

title: An Attention item is cleared by a person
description: Move the Attention item on - note
annotation: Resolving a Blocker lets the work continue.

title: Move the Attention item on
description: Resolve, release or waive an Attention item on the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, choose a state change on the Attention item, such as Resolve.

title: Attention gathers items from every unit
annotation: One list shows what needs notice across the organisation.

title: Open Attention across units
annotation: In the navbar, open Attention. The list shows the items of every unit.

title: The list works like the unit page
description: Move an Attention item from the list - note
annotation: The same state changes are available from the list.

title: Move an Attention item from the list
description: Move an Attention item from the Attention list.
annotation: On the Attention list, choose a state change on an item.

title: Compliance is the state of the Obligations
annotation: The view shows how far the unit has met what the Evidence-Based Model requires.

title: Open the compliance view
description: Open the compliance view of the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, open Compliance. It shows which Obligations are met and which are open.

title: A waiver excuses an Obligation
annotation: A waiver is recorded with a reason, by a person with the authority to excuse it.

title: Record a waiver
annotation: On the compliance view, choose Waive on an Obligation, enter the reason and save.

title: The dashboard summarises the platform
annotation: It shows the counts and states that matter at a glance.

title: Open the dashboard
annotation: In the navbar, open the Dashboard. It summarises the state of the units.

title: Telemetry shows how the platform behaves
annotation: It reports counts and timings of what the platform does.

title: Open Telemetry
annotation: In the navbar, open Telemetry.

title: Every change publishes an event
annotation: Events record what happened, who did it and with which badge.

title: Open Events
annotation: In the navbar, open Events.

title: Version events record each version
annotation: A version event is recorded when an entity reaches a new version.

title: Open Version Events
annotation: In the navbar, open Version Events.
